facts.statement: Parvavis is an extinct enantiornithean bird known from the Upper Cretaceous of China.
facts.quote: Parvavis is a genus of enantiornithean bird, known from the upper Cretaceous (Turonian–Santonian) of China in the Jiangdihe Formation.

facts.statement: The only known species, Parvavis chuxiongensis, was found in Luojumei Village, Chuxiong City, in southern China.
facts.quote: The type and only species, Parvavis chuxiongensis, was recovered in Luojumei Village, Chuxiong City, Yunnan Province, southern China

facts.statement: At the time of its discovery, Parvavis was the only known Mesozoic bird from southern China.
facts.quote: it was the only known Mesozoic bird from south China at the time of its discovery

facts.statement: The skeleton of Parvavis was discovered near Luojumei in Yunnan province, China, in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010, the skeleton of a small bird was found near Luojumei, a village close to the city of Chuxiong in the Yunnan province of China

facts.statement: Parvavis chuxiongensis was formally named and described in 2014 by Wang Min, Zhou Zhonghe, and Xu Guanghui.
facts.quote: in 2014 the type species Parvavis chuxiongensis was named and described by Wang Min, Zhou Zhonghe and Xu Guanghui

facts.statement: The genus name Parvavis combines the Latin words for 'small' and 'bird'.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the Latin prefix “parvus”, which means small, and “avis” which means bird

facts.statement: Parvavis holds the distinction of being the first bird known from the Upper Cretaceous of China and the first Mesozoic bird from Southern China.
facts.quote: Parvavis is the first bird known from the Upper-Cretaceous of China and the first mesozoic bird from Southern China

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was found in lake deposits within the Jiangdihe Formation.
facts.quote: The fossil, holotype IVPP V18586/1, was found in lake deposits of the Jiangdihe formation

facts.statement: The fossil consists of a partially complete, articulated skeleton with skull fragments and feather impressions.
facts.quote: It consists of a partially complete and articulated skeleton with parts of the skull and impressions of feathers on some of the rock

facts.statement: Preserved skeletal elements include the tail, pygostyle, and the back of the skull.
facts.quote: Of the spine, only the tail and pygostyle were preserved, and of the skull only the back

facts.statement: Parvavis was a small bird with a wingspan of approximately 15 centimeters.
facts.quote: Parvavis is, like the genus name suggests, a small bird with a wingspan of about 15 centimeters

facts.statement: A distinguishing feature of Parvavis is that the bottom joint of its second metatarsal is wider than the others.
facts.quote: the bottom joint of the second metatarsal is wider than those of the other metatarsals

facts.statement: Parvavis possessed a reduced claw on its fourth toe.
facts.quote: the fact that the claw on the fourth toe is reduced

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses place Parvavis in a basal position within the Enantiornithes, outside the Longipterygidae family.
facts.quote: Cladistic analyses put Parvavis in a relatively basal position within the Enantiornithes, outside Longipterygidae

facts.statement: The basal position of Parvavis suggests that early enantiornithine forms existed for a longer period than previously thought.
facts.quote: This indicates that these basal forms existed for much longer than previously suspected

facts.statement: Parvavis lived between 93.9 and 83.6 million years ago, during the Turonian to Santonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Santonian (93.9 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Bone structure analysis indicates the holotype individual was nearly fully grown when it died.
facts.quote: Based on its bone structure, the holotype was determined to be nearly fully grown at its time of death

facts.statement: Histological research suggests Parvavis reached near-adult size but remained unusually small for an enantiornithine.
facts.quote: histological research suggests the animal was close to adult size when it died, but that it was unusually small in size for an enantiornithean
